key_insight: Different flow paths can produce the same flow-matching objective but very different SGD variance, so path choice directly affects optimization speed.
engineering_relevance: For practical generative modeling, selecting a variance-reducing path can lower training cost and improve convergence without changing the target distribution.
method: Analyze stochastic-gradient variance induced by different paths $g_t$ in flow matching.
Solve an optimal path-selection problem (PathOpt$_\theta$) under the constraint that paths preserve the same marginals and velocity field.
Derive a sample-estimable equivalent constraint set so candidate paths can be found numerically.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theory plus experiments on Gaussian data, Gaussian mixtures, and real datasets, with an analytically optimal path found for a one-dimensional Gaussian case.
watch_item: Variance reduction must respect the fixed $G(p_t,v_t^\star)$ constraint; otherwise a lower-variance path can actually slow convergence.
paper_title: Same Flow, Different Paths: Variance Reduction in Flow Matching
